title: Tuba records, Barbarin's age and Eddie Anderson
summary: Lucille Higgins' recording, Barbarin joking about not telling his age, and a mention of Eddie Anderson.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I bet I was, but I hate to get my age away.

Sorry. I said, you're very young. You want me to tell my age? I told you I'm like the ladies. Stop telling my age. Don't tell my age no more. How old are you, Paul? I asked me that yesterday. A guy called Paul Boyd. You know Paul Boyd, Constable Paul Boyd. He said, Paul, how old are you? I said, you guess. He guess. I said, uh-uh, you're wrong. I got my papers. He said, you have your papers with you? I said, no, I'll get them though. I said, I'm like the girls. I don't tell my age no more. Good tuba, man. Rich, Paul's sound. Rich, Paul's sound. That almost seemed to me always wonderful. dear I say Eddie Anderson, oh yeah I remember Eddie Anderson, yeah I remember him.
You wanna hear the next one?
No that's alright, you wanna play something else. That's a good tuba play that Bill Moore. That was good.
